name: zapier-partner-lead-status-to-notion

deployments.name: status-trigger

trigger.authentication_note: Solution Partner Operations Tool connection 'work.flowers'. The partner-tool credential lives HERE, on the trigger — the workflow code never calls the partner tool, so it is not in --connections.
trigger.trigger_note: Polling trigger, one run per lead status change. Re-pinned 1.5.0 -> 1.5.3 on 2026-11-24: on 1.5.0 the deployed trigger reported status active with no error but had ZERO runs, while SPOT showed status changes since September (7 of the 9 companies then tracked in Notion were stale). Most likely the same dedupe-on-a-stable-id defect Zapier fixed for project requests in 1.5.2 (ticket 9NPEKP-739EJ). UNVERIFIED until a real status change fires a run; the daily-sweep deployment keeps Notion correct within a day either way.

deployments.description: SPOT referral lead status change -> upsert that lead's Partner Leads row (near-real-time path).

deployments.name: daily-sweep

trigger.authentication_note: Schedule by Zapier needs no connection. SPOT and Notion are bound as connection aliases because both are called from the workflow body.
trigger.params_note: Daily at 8:00 AM account time (Asia/Singapore), an hour before spot-accepted-sweep-to-notion so a request it files on the same day is linked the next morning. Each fire costs 2 SPOT reads + 1 Notion query + one task per changed record.

deployments.description: Daily: read every SPOT referral lead and project request and upsert whatever changed into Partner Leads (backstop + backfill).

deploy.description: Daily sweep of every Zapier SPOT referral lead and project request into the Notion Partner Leads database. One of two deployments of zapier-partner-lead-status-to-notion (source of truth: github.com/work-flowers/zapier-sdk/tree/main/zapier-partner-lead-status-to-notion).

tables.01M86D6X6RPBV57GGHXYKTQ9P8: Partner Leads (SPOT sync) — SPOT id -> Partner Leads page id + last-synced Status / Modified On. OWNED here (created 2026-11-24). The change detector: an unchanged record costs nothing.
tables.01KPZFHX4RP6SER3AEK4YJ62BF: Register Zapier Lead Table — client id -> Company page id, written by register-zapier-partner-lead. Read when creating a referral lead's row (Company link, Source 'Notion CRM').
tables.01JYEPSEARXB2Z6BJRCMFGXBC2: email -> Contact page id, owned by contact-emails-to-zapier-table. Read for the Account Owner link.
tables.01KYV1R8BWAZ697HQ8P1QV80AF: SPOT Project Requests — request id -> Deal/Contact/Company page ids, owned by spot-project-request-to-notion. Read to link a project request's row.
tables.01JM3J9SG5X6S8GBSSC8AS28AT: User IDs — partner contact id -> Notion user id, for the Owner person property.

select_options.Zapier Lead Status: Added 'Converted' (green) and 'Expired' (orange) — the trigger emits five statuses (Submitted, Approved, Converted, Rejected, Expired) and only three had options. Legacy 'Accepted' left in place but never written; the API has never emitted it.

description: Keeps the Notion Partner Leads database in step with Zapier SPOT: one row per referral lead and project request. Two deployments share this source: the SPOT status-change trigger (one lead, near-real-time) and a daily sweep (everything, idempotent via a free Zapier Table cache; also the backfill).
durable_version_note: Pinned to 0.10.1 deliberately. A publish on 0.11.0 failed at run time with 'Dependency installation failed' — the durable runtime's pnpm enforces a minimum release age and 0.11.0 was under a day old (published 2026-07-27T14:58Z). Check the publish date before bumping. Version 019fa7a7-… / 019fa7a8-… are the discarded 0.11.0 publishes.
connections_note: spot = Solution Partner Operations Tool connection 'work.flowers'. The sweep calls SPOT from the body (referral_lead_status_change as a read, find_project_request), so it is bound as an alias; the status-trigger deployment's trigger also holds it as authentication_id.

notion.note: Replaces the Zapier Lead fields on Companies, which this Zap no longer writes.

write_cap: MAX_WRITES_PER_RUN = 60 Notion writes per run; the rest are reported as deferred and picked up next run.
